payload.executive_summary: Candidate B2A selects architecture option O2 (task-parallel fan-out/fan-in) to improve wall-clock throughput while preserving deterministic governance, auditability, role separation, and no-scope-expansion constraints. Delivery is staged via a hybrid milestone plan: Phase 1 proves the end-to-end single-lane spine (intake, workspace governance, audit spine, and sequential execution), Phase 2 introduces limited parallel lanes on a test repo, Phase 3 adds deterministic integration/merge ordering and integration validators/review, and Phase 4 completes Judge/Freeze closure gates and full freeze-bundle assembly. Elevated risks are concentrated in integration conflict handling (K12), workspace integrity under partitioning (K8), and separation-of-powers enforcement across multiple concurrent pods (K10), mitigated by deterministic merge ordering, namespaced workspace partitions, and orchestrator-enforced output/tool allowlists with high HITL strictness.

architecture_choice.rationale: O2 is chosen to reduce wall-clock time for repositories with multiple independent implementation tasks while still meeting all MUST governance and determinism requirements: immutable audit spine (R8), JSON-only canonical artifacts (R9), RFC 6901 evidence pointers (R10/R11), RFC 6902-only repairs for JSON artifacts (R12), diff-only patchsets for code changes (R13), deterministic smallest-passing-repair selection (R15), and no semantic drift without ChangeRequest + escalation (R16). The hybrid rollout de-risks complexity by first validating an O1-like single-lane execution path and workspace/audit controls, then incrementally enabling parallel lanes, and finally adding deterministic fan-in integration (merge ordering + conflict escalation) before enabling full Judge→Freeze closure.
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: Intake & DAG Work Planner (C12) validates plan_package_final.json + repo_context.json + workspace_context.json and initializes run_manifest/event_log/workspace_index via Workspace Manager (C22). Global Orchestrator (C11) fans out lane task slices to Task Lane Orchestrator (C13), which runs per-lane Generate→Validate→Review→Patch with Writer Pool (C14), Per-Lane Validator (C15), Per-Lane Reviewer (C16, findings-only), and Per-Lane Patcher (C17). When lanes complete, Integration Merge Engine (C18) applies lane patchsets to the base repo state in a deterministic order, emitting merged repo_snapshot plus conflict reports as needed; Integration Validator (C19) runs full-repo validation and Integration Reviewer/Patcher (C20/C21) address cross-lane issues. Judge Pod (C23) evaluates integrated outputs and evidence/trace completeness and issues freeze/no-freeze recommendation; Freeze Assembler (C24) produces the Implementation Freeze Bundle (R7/CNS10) only when all closure gates pass (R21), writing final artifacts and stage_handoffs into governed workspace partitions (C22).
key_design_decisions: Adopt O2 fan-out/fan-in with deterministic integration flow rather than purely sequential execution (O1).
Use a hybrid rollout: single-lane foundation first, then limited parallel lanes, then deterministic integration, then full Judge/Freeze closure.
Enforce namespaced workspace partitions (C22) to reduce cross-lane contamination and bound lane context packs.
Define deterministic integration merge ordering that is independent of lane completion timing, with explicit conflict escalation thresholds (K12).
Maintain high HITL strictness for parallel-lane complexity and unresolved merge/patch-format policy details (Q7–Q9).

milestones.name: Phase 1 — Single-lane foundation (O2 backbone validated with O1-like execution)

deliverables.text: Operational single-lane path proving intake validation, audit spine, workspace governance, deterministic context packs, and checkpointed stage_handoffs using O2 components (C11, C12, C22) with a single-lane execution path.

exit_criteria: Stage sequence and checkpoint boundaries demonstrably meet R4/AT4 with stage_handoff emitted at every transition (R5/AT5, R6/AT6).
Intake rejects non-canonical planning inputs and enforces plan_package_final.json as sole authoritative planning input (R1/AT1).
repo_context.json and workspace_context.json schema gates enforced prior to any generation/workspace writing (R2/AT2, R3/AT3).
Audit spine immutability and append-only event log behaviors verified (R8/AT8).
JSON-only canonical outputs and schema enforcement verified (R9/AT9).
Tool permission matrix enforcement and secrets guardrails verified in baseline runs (R19/AT19, R20/AT20).

milestones.name: Phase 2 — Thin-slice parallel lanes on a test repo

deliverables.text: Two parallel lanes executing per-lane Generate→Validate→Review→Patch with enforced role separation (writers vs findings-only reviewers vs patchers) and lane-scoped artifacts/workspace partitions.

exit_criteria: Diff-only patchset artifacts accepted; non-diff mechanisms rejected (R13/AT13).
RFC 6902-only mutation pathway for canonical JSON artifacts enforced (R12/AT12).
Role separation and reviewers findings-only constraints enforced with recorded multi-vendor routing (R22/AT22).
Per-lane validation emits structured results with deterministic AT# mappings where applicable (R25 guidance; validate trace pipeline readiness).

milestones.name: Phase 3 — Deterministic integration: merge ordering, conflict handling, and integrated validation

deliverables.text: Integration Merge/Validate/Review/Patch sub-flow (C18–C21) with deterministic merge ordering and structured conflict reporting/escalation; integrated full-repo validation and trace evidence across lane + integration artifacts.

exit_criteria: Deterministic smallest-passing-repair selection is demonstrably applied when multiple passing repair patchsets exist (R15/AT15).
Evidence pointer compliance is end-to-end across lane and integration outputs; non-compliant evidence formats rejected (R10/AT10, R11/AT11).
No semantic deviations from upstream R#/AT#/O#/K# without ChangeRequest + escalation (R16/AT16).
Integration conflicts are detected and handled via deterministic policy (block/patch/reroute/HITL) with audit log records (K12 mitigation alignment).

milestones.name: Phase 4 — Full closure: Judge gates and Freeze bundle assembly

deliverables.text: Judge→Freeze completion with closure gates enforced and full Implementation Freeze Bundle (R7/CNS10) produced only when all deterministic validators pass (R21).

exit_criteria: Freeze is denied if any closure gate fails; permitted only when all gates pass (R21/AT21).
Freeze bundle contains all required artifacts/directories enumerated in R7 (AT7).
Workspace integrity, indexing completeness, and context pack bounds enforcement validated (R17/AT17, R18/AT18).
Flaky/nondeterministic failure policy enforced with deterministic retries, quarantine/escalation, and audit recording (R23/AT23).

decision_log.question: Which architecture option should this candidate implement: sequential (O1), parallel lanes (O2), checkpoint micro-cycles (O3), or monolith (O4)?
decision_log.choice: Select O2 (task-parallel fan-out/fan-in with deterministic integration sub-flow).
decision_log.rationale: O2 best addresses wall-clock throughput for repos with independent tasks while retaining deterministic governance primitives (audit spine, schema-gated JSON artifacts, evidence pointers, bounded repair loops, and no semantic drift). The staged rollout reduces risk by validating the single-lane governance spine before enabling parallelism and integration complexity.
what_would_change_this_decision: If the target repos are tightly coupled with frequent cross-cutting changes causing high merge conflict rates (K12), favor O1 or O3.
If deterministic partial-freeze/resume is the dominant requirement due to strict budget limits (Q13), favor O3.
If operational simplicity and minimal component surface area is prioritized over modularity and strict internal separation guarantees, consider O4 with stronger emitted handoffs.

decision_log.question: How should O2 be delivered to reduce orchestration and integration risk?
decision_log.choice: Adopt a hybrid milestone strategy: Phase 1 single-lane foundation, Phase 2 thin-slice parallel lanes, Phase 3 integration merge ordering + integrated validation, Phase 4 full Judge/Freeze closure.
decision_log.rationale: Parallel lanes and deterministic integration introduce the highest complexity (merge ordering independence from wall-clock completion, conflict escalation, cross-lane traceability). Incremental enablement allows validating governance invariants (R1–R10, R17–R20) before introducing fan-out/fan-in behaviors and integration-specific hazards (K12, K8, K10).
alternatives_considered: Immediate full O2 implementation (all lanes + integration + freeze gates at once)
Pure O1 first release and defer O2 indefinitely
what_would_change_this_decision: If integration/merge behavior is already provided as a proven deterministic subsystem with existing validators, phases could be collapsed.
If early performance is non-critical, deliver O1 fully before introducing O2.

decision_log.question: How should shared workspace governance be structured under parallel lanes?
decision_log.choice: Use namespaced workspace partitions with a unified workspace_index and an explicit integration partition (C22).
decision_log.rationale: Namespacing reduces cross-lane contamination risk and enables smaller, lane-scoped context packs (mitigating K9) while preserving global auditability via a unified index (R18) and checkpoint-resumability via stage_handoffs (R5/R6).
alternatives_considered: Single shared workspace without partitions (higher collision risk)
Fully isolated per-lane workspaces without a unified index (weaker global traceability and freeze assembly complexity)
what_would_change_this_decision: If the workspace backend cannot support enforceable partitioning/access controls (A6/Q2), revert to a single workspace with stricter forbidden-path and tool sandbox enforcement.
If context packs can be deterministically bounded without partitions and contamination risk is low, partitions may be simplified.

decision_log.question: How should integration apply/merge ordering be handled to preserve reproducibility under parallel completion timing?
decision_log.choice: Require a deterministic merge ordering algorithm independent of lane completion order, with explicit conflict thresholds and structured conflict reports (C18 + K12 mitigation).
decision_log.rationale: O2 reproducibility depends on deterministic outcomes regardless of wall-clock scheduling; merge ordering must be defined as policy/data and enforced by the Integration Merge Engine. Explicit thresholds prevent unsafe or non-deterministic auto-resolution and provide a deterministic escalation path (patch → reroute → HITL → ChangeRequest).
alternatives_considered: Apply patchsets in completion order (non-deterministic across runs)
Allow ad-hoc conflict resolution by integration patcher without explicit thresholds (higher governance risk)
what_would_change_this_decision: If the repo is guaranteed to have non-overlapping file ownership per lane (strong partitioning), merge ordering might be simplified while still deterministic.
If upstream plan defines a strict integration order aligned to module dependencies, merge ordering can be anchored to that DAG order.

decision_log.question: What governance posture should be applied to tool permissions and human-in-the-loop (HITL) under O2 parallelism?
decision_log.choice: Keep tooling sandboxed with deny-by-default network and maintain high HITL strictness for conflicts, security findings, permission expansions, and any semantic deviations.
decision_log.rationale: Parallel lanes increase the surface area for policy violations (K5/K19), role separation failures (K10), and merge conflict escalation (K12). High HITL strictness and sandboxed tooling reduce blast radius and preserve auditability and compliance under increased orchestration complexity.
alternatives_considered: Relax HITL to improve throughput (higher risk of unsafe freezes and policy bypass)
Enable network/package-manager access by default (higher supply-chain and reproducibility risk)
what_would_change_this_decision: If organization provides hardened, deterministic build environments with vetted allowlists and strong automated compliance gates (Q11/Q17), some HITL triggers could be narrowed.
If target repos are low-risk internal prototypes, HITL strictness could be reduced by policy with explicit approval.

decision_log.question: How should the candidate validate core determinism and governance invariants early while still targeting O2 throughput?
decision_log.choice: Gate Phase 1 on core acceptance tests for contracts, audit spine, stage handoffs, JSON-only enforcement, tool permissions, and secrets policy; expand gates as parallelism and integration are enabled.
decision_log.rationale: Early proof of the governance spine ensures later parallel/integration work is built on a validated deterministic foundation; staging acceptance gates reduces the chance of expensive rework when adding lanes and integration.
alternatives_considered: Run only full-suite acceptance at the end (late discovery of foundational issues)
Skip early governance gates in favor of feature delivery (violates policy posture and increases K1/K2/K8 risk)
what_would_change_this_decision: If an existing conformance test harness already verifies R1–R23 for the orchestrator/workspace stack, Phase 1 gating could be lighter and focus on O2-specific aspects.

synthesis_warnings.summary: O2 Phase 3 depends on unresolved blocking specification details (diff format + normalization, smallest-passing-repair scoring/tie-break implementation details beyond R15, and cross-lane conflict resolution/escalation thresholds). These correspond to open questions Q7–Q9 and must be specified deterministically to avoid non-reproducible integration outcomes.

Namespaced workspace partitions (C22) and checkpoint/resume guarantees depend on workspace backend capabilities and constraints (Q2, A6). If backend cannot enforce namespace isolation, append-only semantics, and indexing/retention policies, O2 partitioning may be infeasible without revising the workspace governance approach.
